edges.description: An outside address used a remote desktop gateway to log in to WKSTN-042 as the user jsmith, which is how the intruder first got in.

edges.action: ran hidden commands and checked privileges
edges.description: Once logged in as jsmith, the attacker launched a disguised command line from Outlook and then ran commands to see who they were and whether they had top-level admin rights.
The workstation began quietly sending small bursts of data back to the same outside address every minute, a sign of ongoing remote control.
The attacker dumped the memory of a system process that holds cached passwords, giving them material to impersonate other accounts.
Using the secrets taken from the workstation, the attacker requested a ticket from the domain controller pretending to be the administrator account, without ever knowing the real password.

edges.action: logged into file server as admin
edges.description: Armed with the administrator identity, the attacker connected to the file server and opened a file-sharing session, gaining broad access to company files.

edges.action: ran remote commands and grabbed files
edges.description: The attacker then remotely executed commands on the file server and read sensitive finance and employee records, packaging them into a hidden archive for removal.

edges.action: sent large amount of data out
edges.description: A very large transfer, matching the size of the packaged files, was sent from the file server to an outside address, indicating the stolen data left the network.
The file server contacted the original outside address again, appearing to confirm that the data theft had finished.
Finally, the attacker cleared the security log and deleted the archive file, actions aimed at hiding what had just happened.

summary: An outside address logged into WKSTN-042 as jsmith, then ran hidden commands to explore the machine and steal cached credentials, which were used to impersonate the administrator account on the domain controller and file server; the attacker then read sensitive finance and HR files, packaged them, sent a large amount of data to an external address, and finally cleared logs and deleted the evidence.
